headline: GOLD CRASHES TO 2026 LOW — BLOCKBUSTER JOBS REPORT KILLS FED RATE-CUT HOPES
snippet: Gold fell 3.27% to $4,328 on Friday after May payrolls surged to 172,000 — double the 85,000 consensus — erasing all of gold's 2026 price gains and flipping market bets from cuts to a 69% chance of a Fed hold in June as the Iran oil shock keeps inflation elevated.

headline: COPPER DIVES TOWARD $6.30 AS CHILE POSTS WORST APRIL OUTPUT IN 23 YEARS
snippet: Copper futures slid toward $6.30/lb Friday as Chile reported a 13.8% year-on-year collapse in April output — its weakest April since 2003 — with Escondida down 16% and Collahuasi off 11%, compounding demand fears from the same US jobs shock that hit gold.

headline: ECB CONFIRMS GOLD HAS DETHRONED US TREASURIES AS THE WORLD'S TOP RESERVE ASSET
snippet: The ECB's annual reserve report confirmed gold ended 2025 as the world's single largest reserve asset at 27% of global reserves — overtaking US Treasuries at 22% — sustained by buying from China, Poland, Turkey and India and a 60% gold price surge last year.

headline: COT REPORT: HOW SPECS ARE POSITIONED IN GOLD AND SILVER AFTER THE JOBS-SHOCK SELLOFF
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Commitment of Traders breakdown dissects speculative gold, silver and US dollar index positions following Friday's jobs-driven selloff — essential reading for tracking whether managed money is capitulating or quietly positioning for the next rally leg into summer.

headline: METALS CREEK (MEK) HITS VISIBLE GOLD IN BOTH MAIDEN HOLES AT TIMMINS' OGDEN PROJECT
snippet: Metals Creek Resources (TSX-V: MEK) hit visible gold in its first two drill holes at the Ogden Gold Project — a 50/50 JV with Discovery Silver on the prolific Porcupine-Destor Break in Timmins, with over 8km of strike along one of Canada's most productive gold corridors.

headline: FORGE RESOURCES (FRG) FIRES UP LARGEST-EVER DRILL CAMPAIGN AT YUKON GOLD-COPPER PORPHYRY
snippet: Forge Resources (CSE: FRG) has mobilized rigs for its largest-ever diamond drill program at the Alotta Project in Yukon's Dawson Range Gold Belt, targeting newly identified porphyry anomalies adjacent to a 78-metre intercept of 1.31 g/t gold drilled last season.

headline: SILVER ACADIA (SLA) CUTS 24.8 METRES OF 329 G/T SILVER IN BATHURST MINING CAMP
snippet: Silver Acadia Exploration (CSE: SLA) returned 24.8 metres grading 328.9 g/t silver, 1.0 g/t gold, 1.5% zinc and 2.0% lead at the Nicholas-Denys Project in the Bathurst Mining Camp — confirming high-grade continuity along a 3-kilometre mineralized trend in northern New Brunswick.

headline: NEVADA JUNIOR EXCALIBUR METALS DRILLS 360 G/T SILVER; 100-METRE ZONE REMAINS OPEN AT DEPTH
snippet: Excalibur Metals Corp. intersected 360 g/t silver and 2.03 g/t gold over 1.52 metres at the Bellehelen project in Nevada's Walker Lane Trend, within a 100-metre-wide zone of elevated precious metals mineralization that drilled out and remains open at depth after a 3,122-metre maiden program.

headline: AMERICAS GOLD & SILVER (USAS) COSALÁ INFILL HITS 600 G/T AG OVER 14M — 3X THE RESOURCE GRADE
snippet: Americas Gold and Silver (TSX: USAS) released infill drill results at the Cosalá Complex in Mexico hitting 14.0 metres of 599.8 g/t silver and 0.8% copper — grades two to three times higher than the current resource model — pointing to significant resource upside at an established producing mine.

headline: GOLD MINERS PRINTING $2,500–$3,000/OZ FREE CASH FLOW — AND STILL TRADING AT JUST 0.6X NAV
snippet: With sector AISC averaging $1,744/oz in Q1 2026 and gold near $4,300, senior producers are generating $2,500–$3,000/oz in free cash flow yet still trade at 0.6–0.8x NAV — a disconnect analysts are calling the most persistent valuation anomaly of the current gold cycle and a classic 'buy the boredom' setup.
